title: Dev Saran v. State of U.P. And 4 Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Misra and Shekhar Kumar Yadav, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to Section 127 appeal.
headnote: Where a final assessment of electricity dues has been made, the consumer has a statutory appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003. The High Court disposed of the writ with liberty to avail that remedy and did not examine the assessment or the recovery on merits.
facts: Dev Saran filed a writ in the Allahabad High Court over electricity dues. On 31 August 2020 the Division Bench passed the matter over because counsel could not identify the provision for the provisional assessment or for a fresh final assessment bill, and directed service on counsel for Purvanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. On 22 September 2020 the licensee produced a 31 December 2019 letter from the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II, Fatahan, Mirzapur, seeking recovery of a final assessment of Rs.1,17,804 through the revenue department.

holding_units.topic: relegation to statutory appeal against final assessment
holding_units.holding: It not being in dispute that an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 lies against a final assessment order, the writ petition challenging electricity dues and recovery of that assessment is disposed of with liberty to the consumer to avail the statutory appeal.

principle_tags.application: The Court treated the Executive Engineer's recovery letter as proceeding on a final assessment and, the availability of a Section 127 appeal being undisputed, closed the writ with liberty to appeal.
The writ was not decided on the correctness of the assessment or the recovery; the consumer was relegated to the statutory appeal under Section 127.

not_decided.point: Merits and quantum of the final assessment of Rs.1,17,804
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine whether the assessment was correctly made.

not_decided.point: Statutory basis of the provisional assessment and entitlement to a fresh final assessment bill
not_decided.note: Counsel could not identify the governing provisions on 31 August 2020; the disposing order did not resolve that issue.
